requirements.title: Access and preconditions on the patch maintenance routes
requirements.rationale: Every route here changes the patch list or a branch, so each one must refuse a caller without write access and a workspace that cannot take the write, before it reads or changes anything.

criteria.condition: a request to PATCH or DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id, POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/restore, POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin or POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/reorder comes from a PAT without the scope patches:write, from a caller with read access but not write access, or from a caller with no access to the workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request without changing a patch, moving a ref, contacting origin or emitting an event
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope for the PAT, whether or not the workspace exists; HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden for the caller with read access only; HTTP 404 with error_type not_found, identical to the answer for an unknown slug, for the caller with no access

setup: a patch fixture: a carry-patch workspace 'carry' in status ready in a real store in t.TempDir(), with patches A (branch patch/a), B (patch/b) and C (patch/c) at positions 1, 2, 3, all active, and the real event log of internal/event on the same store
the routes mounted on the real router of internal/server behind the carry-patch route guard of package 31, with a clock the test controls
a recording fetcher in place of the origin fetch
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/maintain_guard_test.go, TestMaintenanceRoutes_RefuseCallersWithoutWriteAccess, a table over the five routes {PATCH /patches/:id, DELETE /patches/:id, POST /patches/:id/restore, POST /patches/reorder, POST /patches/:id/reset-to-origin} times the callers {PAT with only patches:read -> 403 insufficient_scope, PAT with only patches:read on an unknown slug -> 403 insufficient_scope, caller with read access only -> 403 forbidden, user outside the organization -> 404 not_found, owner on an unknown slug -> 404 not_found}: r = send(route, caller, a valid body); assert r.status and r.json.error.error_type; assert list(patches) unchanged; assert events(parley.patch.*) empty; assert fetcher.calls == 0

criteria.condition: a caller with write access sends a request with a valid body to one of the five patch maintenance routes of a workspace whose workspace_mode is standard, a task fork of a carry-patch workspace included
criteria.action: refuse the request without changing a patch, moving a ref or emitting an event
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type workspace_mode_mismatch

requirements.title: Patch update
requirements.rationale: A developer disables, re-enables, marks, describes and moves a patch without re-registering it, and a partial body must never wipe a field it does not name.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access sends PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id for a non-deleted patch with a JSON object carrying description, upstream_pr_url or both
criteria.action: set description and upstream_pr_url from the members that are present and not null, clear a field to null when its member is the empty string, leave every field whose member is absent or null as it was, ignore branch_name and unknown members, set updated_at to now when a field changed, and answer with the patch as it now stands
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the patch object, every field present (null when unset)

requirements.title: Soft delete of a patch
requirements.rationale: Removing a patch must take it out of the next rebuild at once, yet a removal made by mistake has to stay reversible, so neither the row nor the branch nor the backup ref may go.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access sends DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id for a non-deleted patch
criteria.action: set the patch's status to deleted, deleted_at to now, position to null and conflict_files to [], renumber the remaining non-deleted patches 1..N-1 in their existing order, all in one transaction, and leave the patch branch and refs/parley/replaced/<branch> untouched
criteria.contract: HTTP 204 with an empty body; the get route returns the patch with status deleted, position null and deleted_at set; the list route returns the other patches at positions 1..N-1

requirements.title: Restore of a deleted patch
requirements.rationale: A patch removed by a caller, or by a rebuild that judged it merged upstream, must come back with one call while its row still exists.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/restore for a patch whose status is deleted, whether a caller deleted it or a rebuild removed it as merged upstream, and no non-deleted patch of the workspace has the same branch_name
criteria.action: set the patch's status to active, its position to N+1 where N is the number of non-deleted patches before the call, deleted_at to null and conflict_files to [], in one transaction, and answer with the patch
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the patch object: status active, position the last of the list, deleted_at null, conflict_files []

requirements.title: Patch reorder and the gap-free order
requirements.rationale: Rebuilds apply patches in position order, so the order has to be settable in one step and can never be left with a gap, a duplicate or a patch missing from it.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/reorder with patch_ids naming every non-deleted patch of the workspace exactly once
criteria.action: renumber the patches 1..N in the order of patch_ids in one transaction, set updated_at on each patch whose position changed, and answer with all non-deleted patches in the new order
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {items: list of patch objects in the order of patch_ids at positions 1..N, next_cursor: null}

requirements.title: CLI command that resets a patch to origin and waits for the rebuild
requirements.rationale: A script that resets a patch usually wants to know whether the integration branch rebuilt, so the command can follow the job the reset queued and report both in one document.

criteria.contract: stdout is the hub's response as one JSON document; exit status 0; a hub error is printed on stderr as received with exit status 1

criteria.condition: a user runs parley patch reset-to-origin <workspace-slug> <patch-id> --wait and the hub's response names a rebuild_job_id
criteria.action: poll GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/rebuilds/<rebuild_job_id> through the shared wait until the job's status is completed, dead_letter or cancelled, treating queued, running and failed as not terminal, and print one document: the reset response with one more member, rebuild, holding the final job record
criteria.contract: stdout is one JSON document: every member of the reset response plus rebuild: the final job record; exit status 0 when the job's status is completed

execution_paths.title: A developer maintains the patch list from the shell

steps.action: runs parley patch update carry <B> --status disabled on a carry-patch workspace with the patches A, B, C at positions 1, 2, 3
sends PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/carry/patches/<B> with {status: 'disabled'} and the developer's API key
authenticates the caller, finds write access and a ready carry-patch workspace, sets B to disabled, writes parley.patch.update in the same transaction and answers 200 with the patch
checks that the three ids are every non-deleted patch exactly once, renumbers them 1, 2, 3 in that order, writes one parley.patch.reorder and answers 200 with the items in the new order
soft-deletes C, renumbers A and B to 1 and 2, writes parley.patch.delete and answers 204
makes C active at position 3 with deleted_at null, writes parley.patch.restore and answers 200 with the patch
runs parley patch list carry and reads A at 1, B at 2 and disabled, C at 3 and active

a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its real router, authentication and access middleware
the patch routes of internal/carrypatch, those of package 31 included

an origin and an upstream repository served by internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest, origin holding the branches patch/a, patch/b and patch/c
the carry-patch workspace 'carry' created through POST /api/v1/workspaces and waited for until ready, and the three patches registered through parley patch add as package 31 specifies
end_state: parley patch list carry prints three patches at positions 1, 2, 3: patch/a active, patch/b disabled, patch/c active with deleted_at null

every command exited 0 and printed exactly one JSON document on stdout

execution_paths.title: A developer forces a diverged patch branch back to origin's tip

steps.action: runs parley patch reset-to-origin carry <A> after the hub's patch/a and origin's patch/a each gained a commit the other lacks
sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/carry/patches/<A>/reset-to-origin with the developer's API key
authenticates the caller, finds write access, a ready carry-patch workspace and an active patch, resolves the origin credential and fetches the branch patch/a from origin
serves its tip of patch/a to the fetch
finds the tips diverged, saves its own tip to refs/parley/replaced/patch/a and moves refs/heads/patch/a to origin's tip by compare-and-swap
writes parley.patch.reset and parley.patch.replace, asks for a rebuild when auto_rebuild_after_sync is true, and answers 200 with the patch, action replaced and replaced_sha
prints the answer on stdout and exits 0
runs parley patch show carry <A> and reads replaced_sha, the tip the hub discarded

a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its real router, authentication and access middleware

the carry-patch workspace 'carry' created and ready, with patch/a registered as patch A, as in the first end-to-end test of this file

one commit added to patch/a in the hub's bare repository <[workspace].path>/carry.git with git, and a different commit pushed to patch/a on origin, so that the tips diverge; H is the hub's tip and O origin's

git rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a in the hub's bare repository prints O
git rev-parse refs/parley/replaced/patch/a in the hub's bare repository prints H
